messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: custom text in the middle of a donut plot
parts:
Hi Daniel,

On Thu, Mar 7, 2013 at 1:16 PM, Daniel Bowen
<bowenter...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi. I don't think this requires sample code, so I'll just ask first.

Sample code makes things easier, even for simple examples.

>
> I attached a donut plot I created using geom_rect(). The plot displays a
> calorie profile I've defined: how much I've consumed (dark colors) and how
> much I have left to consume (light colors). I want to put text in the middle
> of the plot. specifically - as I have the total Fat Carbs and Protein
> consumed in the ylab(), I'd like to put the total in the middle of the plot
> [ ... "480 / 2000 Calories"].
>
> I suspect this is possible. Maybe with ?annotate?, or possibly some other
> means. I figured I might place some text on the plot with coordinates, but
> the coordinates are polar(???). I'm just a lil stuck.

What did you try? You seem to be on the right track. In polar
coordinates center is usually 0,0 so

annotate(geom="text", label="hello world", x = 0, y=0)

seems like the first thing to try.

Best,
Ista
>
> Thank you, in advance.
>
> Dan
